name: Colorado
summary: Statutes and Constitution: the Office of Legislative Legal Services publishes the full 2026 C.R.S. (and Constitution as 'title-00') as one HTM/PDF/DOCX file per title on olls.info, plus whole-code zips — read them with fetch_doc.py or a corpus, since each file is millions of characters; public.law (per-section, 2024 text) and Justia (2025) are the WebFetch-friendly fallbacks, and the legislature's own C.R.S. link is a LexisNexis JS app. Court rules have no free consolidated text except LexisNexis (JS, link-only); coloradojudicial.gov hosts only rule-change orders. CCR is official on sos.state.co.us (shell gets HTTP 500; search paths robots-disallowed) with Cornell LII as a stale mirror. Case law: coloradojudicial.gov announcement sheets (published and unpublished COA decisions, SC opinions, cert denials) are reachable by WebFetch but the shell is IP-banned (403); full opinion text is most reliably read on Justia (with ¶ numbers); the judiciary's research.coloradojudicial.gov archive is a vLex JS app.

citation_map.notes: C.R.S. section numbers are title-article-section, each part may carry a decimal (25.5-4-301, 24-71.5-104, 13-80-102.5); the olls.info file key is the TITLE only (two-digit padded: 01-09; 25.5, 26.5 keep the dot). Colorado style puts C.R.S. after the number ('section 13-80-102(1)(a), C.R.S. 2025'); the regex requires 'C.R.S.' or 'Colo. Rev. Stat.' before the number or after a comma — a bare 'N-N-N' or '§ 13-80-102' with no C.R.S. tag must not route here. Ranges ('C.R.S. §§ 13-80-101 to -103') match only the first section. Rule cites: 'Crim. P.' and 'C.R.E.' are Colorado-specific, but bare 'Rule 12' or 'Rule 702' must not route here without 'C.R.C.P.', 'CRE' or 'Colorado Rules of …'; Fed. R. … forms are excluded. Public-domain citations (YYYY CO N / YYYY COA N, ¶ pinpoints) began in 2012 (from memory); P.3d is a West reporter, Colorado Reports and Colo. App. reports ended in 1980 (from memory). Docket forms: YYCA#### (COA), YYSC### (cert petitions/review), YYSA### (original proceedings), YYPDJ### (disciplinary) — generic, route only with Colorado context. Unpublished COA decisions are announced as 'NOT PUBLISHED PURSUANT TO C.A.R. 35(e)'; whether and from what date they may be cited (C.A.R. 35(e) amendment) was not verified. Register cite 'VV CR NN, date' — regex requires the date to avoid colliding with other 'CR' abbreviations. CourtListener ids from memory, unverified. The C.R.S. regex also accepts 'CRS N-N-N' and 'Colorado Revised Statutes § N-N-N', and prose 'section N-N-N of the Colorado Revised Statutes' (added after the independent check). The court's own opinion listing writes '26CO65' with no spaces; the public-domain regex accepts a two-digit year and no spaces. Bare 'Crim. P.' excludes any preceding 'X.' abbreviation and 'Unified' (Maine's M.R.U. Crim. P.) (2026-10-17).

sources.title: Colorado Revised Statutes — OLLS title downloads (HTM / PDF / DOCX)
sources.publisher: Colorado General Assembly, Office of Legislative Legal Services (Revisor of Statutes)
sources.official_status_evidence: Download page (content.leg.colorado.gov/agencies/office-legislative-legal-services/2026-crs-titles-download) carries no official/unofficial statement; the legislature's C.R.S. page sends readers to the LexisNexis-hosted C.R.S. Colorado adopted UELMA (C.R.S. 24-71.5-101 et seq., HB 12-1209) but no authentication statement was seen on these files.
sources.coverage: All C.R.S. titles 1-44 (incl. 25.5, 26.5), the Colorado Constitution (title-00) and the general index, 2026 edition, with editor's notes and case annotations interleaved. One file per title; prior editions exist (crs2024 on content.leg.colorado.gov/sites/default/files/images/olls/; olls.info/crs-archive/ is robots-disallowed).

access.pattern_rules: year = edition year (2026 current; the 2025 edition is no longer at the old leg.colorado.gov path). title = C.R.S. title number zero-padded to two digits for 1-9 (title-01 … title-09, title-13, title-44); decimal titles keep the dot (title-25.5, title-26.5); title-00 = Colorado Constitution; crs{year}-index.pdf = general index. The whole title is one file: locate the section inside it by searching for '{title}-{article}-{section}.' followed by the catchline (e.g. '13-80-102. General limitation of actions - two years.'). The title's opening table of contents lists every article WITH its section range (e.g. 'Art. 80 … 13-80-101 to …'). Verified on 13-80-102 (title-13) and 18-3-102 (title-18), and Colo. Const. art. II, § 25 (title-00).
access.navigation: download page → per-title HTM/PDF/DOCX links (all on olls.info/crs/) → search the file for the section number + catchline.

automation.notes: Files are huge (title 13: 1,769-page PDF, 5.8M chars; HTM 4.6M chars; title 24 PDF 4,892 pp), far past WebFetch's ~100K window, so the fetch tool can't reach most sections. The script route (fetch_doc.py grep/verify/section) is primary; HTM and PDF can both be quoted (fetch_doc.py now decodes the windows-1252 HTM correctly: title-13.htm has 6,090 '§' and no U+FFFD). WebFetch on olls.info is gated: the session permission prompt timed out, which is not a site refusal.
